steps.title: Prepare GRIN lens and EEG wires
steps.instruction: Cut piano wires to ~5 mm, position two on the side of the GRIN lens with a 3 × 5 mm piece of Scotch tape under the microscope so that the tips extend 200–300 µm beyond the lens; add 1–3 µL Krazy glue, let dry, then remove the tape and store the assembled lens. Cut stainless‑steel and silver wires to ~2 cm, strip ~0.3 mm insulation from the ends, solder three stainless‑steel wires (EEG) and two silver wires (EMG) to a 5‑position connector, apply epoxy adhesive around the solder joints, and store the completed electrode assembly.

substeps.instruction: Cut piano wires (~5 mm) and tape them to the GRIN lens.
Apply 1–3 µL Krazy glue, wait to dry, remove tape.
Cut stainless‑steel and silver wires (~2 cm) and strip ends.
Solder three stainless‑steel wires and two silver wires to the connector.
Apply epoxy adhesive around solder area and store.

steps.title: Perform viral injection
steps.instruction: Pull a glass capillary into a needle shape with a Sutter P‑1000, load ~500 nL AAV1‑FLEX‑GCaMP6f into the nano‑injector pipette, anesthetize the mouse with ketamine (100 mg/kg) and xylazine (10 mg/kg) IP, lubricate eyes with ophthalmic ointment, mount on a stereotaxic frame, clip a 1 × 2 cm patch of hair, maintain normothermia on a feedback‑controlled heating pad, disinfect skin three times with povidone‑iodine alternating with 70 % alcohol and finish with povidone‑iodine, remove dorsal skin, level the skull, drill a 1 mm diameter hole at bregma –6.9 mm AP, 1.1 mm lateral, then lower the nano‑injector to 5.6 mm depth, inject 200 nL virus at 50 nL/min, wait 5 min, and slowly retract the injector.

substeps.instruction: Pull glass capillary, load ~500 nL virus.
Anesthetize mouse (ketamine 100 mg/kg, xylazine 10 mg/kg).
Apply ophthalmic ointment, mount in stereotaxic frame, clip hair.
Maintain body temperature, disinfect skin, remove skin.
Drill 1 mm hole at target coordinates (bregma –6.9 mm AP, 1.1 mm L).
Lower injector to 5.6 mm depth, inject 200 nL at 50 nL/min.
Wait 5 min, then retract injector slowly.

steps.title: Implant GRIN lens
steps.instruction: Insert a custom stainless‑steel pin (400 µm diameter, 20 mm length, tip polished) 400 µm above the injection site, leave for 2 min then retract; attach the GRIN lens to an Inscopix holder via the provided adapter, mount the holder on a micromanipulator, lower the lens at 10 µm/s until it is 200 µm above the target coordinate, fix the lens to the skull with minimal black dental cement, and allow the cement to cure for at least 20 min.

substeps.instruction: Insert metal pin 400 µm above injection site, wait 2 min, retract.
Attach GRIN lens to holder and mount on micromanipulator.
Insert lens at 10 µm/s to 200 µm above target.
Secure lens with minimal black dental cement.
Let cement dry ≥20 min.

steps.title: Implant EEG and EMG electrodes
steps.instruction: Trim stainless‑steel and silver wires as needed, strip ~0.3 mm insulation from each end, drill three 0.5 mm diameter skull holes (EEG1: 1 mm from midline, 1.5 mm anterior to bregma; EEG2: 1 mm from midline, 1.5 mm posterior to bregma; reference: cerebellum), insert the EEG stainless wires into the first two holes and secure with bone screws by turning 2.5–3 turns for epidural placement, insert two EMG silver wires bilaterally into neck musculature, cover the skull, GRIN lens, and electrodes with black dental cement, attach a metal headpost with dental cement, and seal the top of the GRIN lens with a silicon adhesive (e.g., Kwik‑Cast). Keep the mouse on a heat pad until it recovers.

substeps.instruction: Trim and strip wires (~0.3 mm).
Drill three 0.5 mm holes at specified coordinates.
Insert EEG wires, secure with bone screws (2.5–3 turns).
Insert EMG wires into neck muscles.
Cover everything with black dental cement.
Attach metal headpost with cement.
Seal GRIN lens top with silicon adhesive.
Maintain mouse on heat pad until recovery.

steps.title: Mount baseplate for imaging
steps.instruction: After 3–4 weeks, secure the awake mouse on a custom head‑fixation platform, attach the baseplate to the bottom of the Inscopix miniature microendoscope, remove the silicon cover from the GRIN lens, position the microendoscope above the lens, adjust the head angle until the focal plane is parallel to the lens surface, locate the optimal focal plane by maximizing cell count and using DF/F mode, cement the baseplate to the skull with black dental cement (do not move the microendoscope until the cement is fully dry), then remove the microendoscope and cover the GRIN lens with the baseplate cover, and return the mouse to its home cage.

substeps.instruction: Fix mouse on head‑fixation platform.
Attach baseplate to microendoscope.
Remove silicon cover from GRIN lens.
Position microendoscope above lens and align angle.
Find optimal focal plane (max cells, DF/F mode).
Secure baseplate with dental cement; wait until dry.
Remove microendoscope and place baseplate cover.
Return mouse to home cage.

steps.title: Record calcium imaging and EEG/EMG
steps.instruction: On the recording day, connect the microendoscope and EEG/EMG cables to the mouse on the head‑fixation platform, habituate the mouse in the behavioral arena for ≥90 min, then acquire calcium imaging for 1–2 h using nVista 3.0 hardware and IDPS software with 475 nm LED illumination at 10 Hz and 0.4–1.2 mW/mm², while simultaneously recording EEG/EMG band‑pass filtered (0.5–500 Hz) and digitized at 1,017 Hz with a Neuralynx Digital Lynx 4S controlled by custom MATLAB code; synchronize the two systems with a TTL pulse from the Inscopix system to the Neuralynx system, and repeat 2–3 imaging sessions to capture wake and sleep states.

substeps.instruction: Connect microendoscope and EEG/EMG cables.
Habituate mouse ≥90 min in arena.
Start calcium imaging (475 nm LED, 10 Hz, 0.4–1.2 mW/mm²).
Record EEG/EMG (0.5–500 Hz, 1,017 Hz) via Neuralynx.
Synchronize recordings with TTL pulse.
Perform 2–3 imaging sessions to capture wake and sleep.

steps.title: Perfuse for histology (optional)
steps.instruction: After recordings, perfuse the mouse and process brain tissue to verify viral expression and GRIN lens placement.
